$comment: Site-owned presentation and curation metadata over two deployment-gated contracts: SDK-owned artifacts/evidence and explicit site-owned exceptions. Version, source, provenance, freshness, health, and integrity come from those contracts rather than this narrative manifest.

projection.ownership: The site owns ordering, narrative, routes, and presentation. The SDK owns executable source, the versioned projection, browser artifacts, and evidence.

currentArtifact.notice: The flagship map page (demo.html) runs live on the @honua/sdk-js 0.2.10 npm browser bundle, vendored byte-for-byte and loaded with the producer's published SRI. The Overture GeoParquet lab (demo-overture.html) consumes the 0.1.2-beta.0 ec58b44 SDK projection, runtime artifact, and producer evidence. Every remaining visible transition is an explicit site-owned exception with commit-pinned source, content digests, CSP/attribution admission checks, and an unavailable live-evidence state when no producer observation exists. Evidence older than seven days is visibly stale; a fixture is never substituted as a live claim.

demoCenter.$comment: Curated order of the demos.html sections. countyJourneys are the County of Maui journeys hosted at samples.honua.io; flagships are at most six maintained developer demos on this site (docs/demo-samples-architecture.md). scripts/site-demo-smoke.mjs asserts demos.html matches each list in order.

executionStates.label: Fixture
executionStates.description: Deterministic bundled data; no live-service claim.

executionStates.label: Public live
executionStates.description: Reads a public upstream endpoint without a Honua account.

executionStates.label: Demo live
executionStates.description: Reads the deployed demo.honua.io service and reports runtime availability.

executionStates.label: Authenticated
executionStates.description: Requires caller-supplied credentials; no credentials are embedded in this site.

executionStates.label: Degraded
executionStates.description: A live capability is unavailable and the experience says what was reduced.

executionStates.label: Unavailable
executionStates.description: The required source or capability is not currently usable.

executionStates.label: Stale evidence
executionStates.description: The last retained observation is older than the seven-day publication window; its status remains visible but is not a current-health claim.

journeys.title: One layer, five doors
journeys.userProblem: I already have GIS services and need one application contract instead of protocol-specific rewrites.
journeys.outcome: Send one zoning selection through GeoServices REST, OGC API Features, and OData and compare identical results, then see the same layer as OGC API Tiles vector tiles and as an OGC API Maps server-rendered PNG of the current view.
differentiators: five standard doors on one layer

execution.runtimeState: The page probes the live server. The three query doors fall back to labelled sample data; the tile and map doors have no sample substitute and say so. Each door shows its request and a one-line result summary (rows, tiles, image bytes).

journeys.title: Put a map on the page
journeys.userProblem: I need a live, styled, clickable map of real data in a web page without an account, a key, or a bundler.
journeys.outcome: Draw Maui zoning by category with a legend from OGC API Tiles, click any of 51,245 parcels for a FeatureServer query through @honua/sdk-js 0.2.10, and fly to an address with the server's geocoder — then copy the twenty lines that do it.
differentiators: vector tiles + feature query from one server

execution.runtimeState: The page reads demo.honua.io live (OGC API Tiles MVT, FeatureServer query, GeocodeServer, PMTiles basemap). If the server is unreachable it draws a labelled Kahului fixture; a missing basemap archive leaves a dark background with a visible chip; geocoding has no fixture and reports unavailable.

journeys.title: A full web map app from the JS SDK
journeys.userProblem: I need the controls people expect from a web map app (layers, legend, basemaps, search, popups, compare, measure, time, filters, share) without writing them myself.
journeys.outcome: Run a Maui web map where every control is an @honua/sdk-js 0.2.10 element or function on live demo.honua.io data, read the wiring, then see every SDK entry point grouped by job.
differentiators: every control is an SDK element
one filter model for tiles and the server

execution.runtimeState: The page reads demo.honua.io live (OGC API Tiles MVT, FeatureServer query and extent, GeocodeServer, PMTiles archives). A failed layer or service is named in the status pill and layer note; nothing falls back to a fixture.

journeys.title: Query 656 MB without downloading it
journeys.userProblem: I need to explore large public GeoParquet in a browser without loading the whole object or hiding what the engine actually read.
journeys.outcome: Run one bounded Oahu query, render results progressively, and inspect measured range, memory, provenance, cache, and timing evidence.
differentiators: self-hosted DuckDB worker, WASM, and extension

execution.runtimeState: The route defaults to a same-origin 1.9 KB fixture with zero cross-origin requests. Selecting AWS explicitly runs the same bounded plan against the pinned anonymous 656,568,610-byte Overture object; rows scanned and row groups pruned remain visibly unverified because DuckDB does not expose them.

journeys.title: Run spatial analytics on the server, paint GeoJSON in the browser
journeys.userProblem: I need clustering, joins, buffers, and binning over my layers without a desktop GIS or a client-side analysis engine.
journeys.outcome: Send DBSCAN clustering, a spatial join to zoning, a 1 km buffer-aggregate, and hex binning to demo.honua.io, see each exact request, and paint every GeoJSON result in its own MapLibre layer.
differentiators: entitlement state read live, never faked

execution.runtimeState: The page reads policies.entitlements from the demo capability manifest at load; an analysis the manifest reports inactive, or whose data provider answers 501, renders disabled with the server's reason; H3 runs only on a managed-store layer, so the page probes maui-buildings-managed then maui-inspections-scratch and the first 200 becomes the H3 target (source-mode layers answer 501), and density is always bounded to the view.

demoGate.outcome: Four server-side analyses return GeoJSON and paint on one map with the exact request shown.
demoGate.dataMode: demo-live (maui-inspections synthetic demo data and its managed scratch copy maui-inspections-scratch, maui-zoning, maui-buildings)
demoGate.producerCommit: the honua-site commit that ships this route; route and assets are content-digested in assets/samples/site-exceptions.v1.json (id spatial-analytics-flagship)
demoGate.evidence: Observed 2026-10-24 from a headless browser: clusters 200 (28 features), spatial-join 200 (28), buffer-aggregate 200 (1), view-bounded density 200 (159-250 hexes, 3-5 s); h3 402 entitlement-inactive, then (licensing disabled, all entitlements active) h3 501 on every source-mode layer. After the h3 extension landed (2026-10-24T22:12Z probe): maui-buildings-managed 404 (not published), maui-inspections-scratch h3 200 at resolutions 5-8 (11/18/25/26 cells, ~0.3 s); the page uses resolution 6 on the scratch layer.
demoGate.degradation: Inactive entitlements disable their button with the manifest reason, and when no H3 candidate answers 200 (source-mode layers answer 501) the H3 button is disabled with the server detail; failed calls show HTTP status and problem detail; an unavailable PMTiles basemap leaves a labeled dark background. No fixture result is substituted.

journeys.title: Inspect and edit field records
journeys.userProblem: Field and office staff need current inspection records and must see exactly what a save sends, without risking shared data.
journeys.outcome: Read Maui field inspections live over OData, edit one, and see the save as the literal PATCH request; when live writes are off the edit stays in the browser and is labelled that way.
differentiators: every save shown as its request
write entitlement read from the server

execution.runtimeState: The page reads inspections live from demo.honua.io and reads the server's write entitlement; without live writes, edits stay local and are labelled.

journeys.title: Maui in 3D: buildings, terrain, imagery
journeys.userProblem: I need imagery, elevation, and 3D building context from one server without building separate data clients for each source.
journeys.outcome: Extrude Overture building footprints over 3DEP terrain with hillshade and NAIP imagery, each layer reporting its own live or degraded state.
differentiators: one server for vectors, rasters, and terrain

execution.runtimeState: Each terrain, imagery, and building layer reports availability separately.

journeys.title: Move an ArcGIS file without rewriting the application
journeys.userProblem: I need a credible, incremental path away from ArcGIS-specific imports and services.
journeys.outcome: Compare the original file with codemod output, then inspect a migrated layer running against an open Honua endpoint.

execution.runtimeState: The migrated map reports endpoint failure instead of substituting fabricated results.
